review: Second-review of five already-executed current B regressions. Read the current worktree source, tests and logs; inspect effective primary PDF 2.0 + EC3 text and fixture construction. This is a bounded input-validity/oracle review, not a new run or whole-clause certification.

cases.source_location: ISO 32000-2 sponsored EC3 PDF physical pp.830–831 / printed pp.815–816: an out-of-MediaBox Crop/Bleed/Trim/Art box shall be treated as its intersection with MediaBox. The immediately preceding phrase says such boxes should not ordinarily extend beyond MediaBox (a producer recommendation, not an invalidity rule). Table 31 is physical pp. 119-120 / printed pp. 104-105; ViewArea/ViewClip are Table 147 and their values include the selected page boundary.
cases.fixture: crates/pdf-model/tests/page_geometry.rs::a_disjoint_page_boundary_clips_all_content_instead_of_defaulting_to_the_medium; page_and_catalog builds a PDF 1.7 one-page exact-xref file for each box. MediaBox is [0,0,100,50], each tested box is a proper ordered, positive-area rectangle, and the disjoint case is [120,10,150,40]. ViewerPreferences explicitly fixes ViewArea=MediaBox and ViewClip to that box, retaining a nonempty 100x50 target while testing empty intersection. The adjacent [50,10,150,40] overlap case tests actual clipping. The page resource/content dictionaries are present; the test checks no recovery and a rendered output.
cases.fixture_validity: Valid reader input. Although disjoint boundaries are not ordinary writer output, §14.11.2.1 explicitly states processor behavior for any extension beyond MediaBox. The range boxes are nondegenerate and the distinction between absent/default and present/disjoint is observable.
cases.oracle: Independent of page-box production helpers: literal page dimensions, pixel-painted booleans, and a distinct partial-overlap control. Failure is opaque content in every disjoint case; the four partial-overlap controls first prove clipping to an intersection. Exact xrefs, no recovery and complete interpretations are explicit.
cases.execution: boundary-font-annotation-wave14.log and later full waves: all four disjoint cases paint where expected output is blank; partial-overlap controls pass.
cases.decision_recheck: The test directly addresses ADR 0414's fallback decision. Table 31 absence defaults do not supersede the explicit intersection instruction for a present value. Keeping ViewArea at MediaBox avoids relying on implementation policy for a zero-sized output target.
cases.residuals: No defect claim for malformed/inverted rectangles, zero-area boundaries, defaulted absent keys, alternative ViewArea choices, or imposition/print semantics.

cases.source_location: Table 74 is physical p. 236 / printed p. 221: required Type 1 pattern /BBox boundaries shall clip the pattern cell; NOTE 1 says zero height or width still paints one pixel. §7.9.5 is physical p. 134 / printed p. 119; its rectangle note permits zero width/height. §10.7.4 is physical p. 399 / printed p. 384: a zero-width/height rectangle paints a one-pixel line for scan conversion.
cases.fixture: crates/pdf-model/tests/degenerate_tiling_bbox_clip_spec_audit.rs::a_zero_height_pattern_bbox_clips_distant_cell_marks_but_scan_converts_its_boundary. PDF 1.7 exact-xref, one page with MediaBox and Resources, valid colored Type 1 tiling pattern (PaintType 1), positive XStep/YStep, empty pattern Resources, and a nondegenerate cell mark. Only BBox height changes from ordinary [0,0,10,10] to [0,5,10,5]. The stream Length is computed from its bytes. The source explicitly allows a degenerate rectangle, so zero height is not an invalid producer fixture.
cases.fixture_validity: Valid input for this specific note. The test does not depend on an omitted-resource fallback or malformed cell stream. The degenerate BBox's boundary is retained as clipping geometry; the regular pattern period remains positive.
cases.oracle: The ordinary control paints the same cell. The degenerate case requires a nontransparent boundary pixel somewhere in the scan-converted boundary band (without pinning ownership to one exact row), while requiring the independently chosen cell pixel two units away to remain transparent. This separates the zero-area scan-conversion note from the required clipping rule and avoids implementation-specific half-open-edge selection.
cases.execution: pattern-syntax-wave15.log and later full waves: ordinary control and boundary-band predicate pass; distant pixel is red/opaque rather than transparent.
cases.decision_recheck: ADR 0056's rationale equating 'paints one pixel' with dropping the clip is not supported: Table 74 separately requires use of BBox as clipping boundaries. The note defines boundary scan conversion, not an unlimited cell region.
cases.residuals: Only zero-height is executed; zero-width is the analogous untested branch. The exact edge row and all rasterization cases are not claimed.

cases.source_location: Table 65 physical p. 206 / printed p. 191; Tables 66-68 physical pp. 207-208 / printed pp. 192-193. Table 65 permits later-version profiles and requires Alternate when the processor cannot process them. For Alternate mapping, source values are constrained to ICCBased range first, then to Alternate range without error. Tables 67-68 include Lab profile data and Lab component ranges.
cases.fixture: crates/pdf-model/tests/icc_alternate_range_spec_audit.rs::unsupported_icc2_profile_clamps_to_icc_range_before_wider_alternate. The embedded 528-byte ICC.2:2023 v5 Lab profile is a valid later ICC version; it is a display-class Lab profile with required forward/reverse MPE transforms. PDF 2.0 stream uses /N 3, an ICC Lab /Range [0 100 -128 127 -128 127] matching the profile's component range, and a valid Lab Alternate whose explicit range extends a* to [-200,200]. Profile bytes are ASCIIHex encoded with matching stream Length. ICC's iccDEV 2.3.2.5 validator independently returned OK/no report; generator and binary hash are preserved in scratchpad/r2038/spec-audit/colour_spaces_current/drafts. The PDF is PDF 2.0 with equal 16-byte trailer IDs and exact xrefs.
cases.fixture_validity: Valid PDF 2.0 writer input. The profile is later-version but later ICC versions are expressly allowed; the reader may be unable to process it and in that case Alternate is the prescribed fallback. /Range values match the ICC Lab range, and the wider Alternate makes the two required clipping stages distinguishable. Page, resources, contents and ICC stream framing are supplied; no recovery is used.
cases.oracle: Strong relational oracle for the tested fallback stage: same public paint path compares profile input [50,150,0] with direct Alternate [50,127,0], then proves the control at [50,150,0] differs. Thus an omitted first clamp is visible. Limitation: the PDF pixel is compared to a direct Lab rendering through the same renderer, rather than an independently implemented colorimetric pixel oracle; the literal source-derived expected value is the effective component [50,127,0]. The 2-level blue delta is from the executed log, not a standalone analytic Lab-to-RGB oracle.
cases.execution: icc-alternate-wave18.log, nine-crate-wave27.log, and later full waves: un-clamped profile fallback RGB [255,0,128], clamped direct-Lab control [255,0,126]; direct controls differ and target equality fails.
cases.decision_recheck: The input chooses a permitted later ICC version and an unsupported MPE tag route, rather than an invalid malformed profile. The fallback clause is explicitly conditional on inability to process the profile. The changed pixel is two output levels and should be reported as a failure of this implemented fallback route, not generalized to profiles the reader successfully supports.
cases.residuals: No claim for supported ICC versions, all later ICC profiles, or independent validation of final RGB conversion. The existing ICC file/generator/ICC validator provide the profile-validity evidence.

cases.source_location: Table 401 physical p. 836 / printed p. 821 gives OutputIntent fields; physical p. 839 / printed p. 824 says output intents are informational and may be disregarded, but if a processor respects them, the page-associated output intent shall be used. The immediately preceding registered-condition text makes Info and DestOutputProfile required only when OutputConditionIdentifier does not specify a standard condition. Example 1 identifies CGATS TR 001 in the ICC Characterization Data Registry.
cases.fixture: crates/pdf-model/tests/output_intent_page_scope_spec_audit.rs. Exact-xref PDF 2.0 fixture has valid /ID, page-level OutputIntents, and a distinct catalog-level custom GRACoL intent backed by the shipped registered GRACoL ICC profile. The page intent names standard CGATS TR 001, supplies /RegistryName and human-readable output condition, and intentionally omits profile because Table 401 allows omission for a recognized standard condition. Page content/resource setup and profile stream are present. Test contrasts page-only, catalog-only, and both; second test separately checks public in_force_on_pages results.
cases.fixture_validity: Valid PDF 2.0 data. A page-level output intent is allowed in PDF 2.0. The catalog's custom intent supplies Info and DestOutputProfile, while page's registered condition supplies its RegistryName and is the standard Example 1 production condition; its missing profile is expressly optional. No external registry access is expected.
cases.oracle: The public condition-report assertion is literal and independent: Catalog GRACoL must not appear in force on a page whose own intent takes priority. The render control compares pixel output with page-only and catalog-only data, proving those alternatives differ; when the processor's intent-aware path respects the page intent, both-intents output should match page-only. This establishes scope/selection failure, not a general colorimetric transform oracle.
cases.execution: output-intents-wave29.log and later full waves: page-only/catalog-only differ; both-intents output follows catalog [96,97,97] rather than page-only [64,64,64]. The public condition report also returns Catalog GRACoL for the page.
cases.decision_recheck: The source explicitly leaves a processor free to disregard output intents. The regression is conditional on this product choosing to use the output-intent route; within that route, page scope is mandatory. It does not require a registry fetch or prescribe conversion when the page profile is unavailable.
cases.residuals: No claim that all PDF readers must honor intents, that a registered condition must be fetched, or that the observed RGB is a universal standard answer. No separate assertion of a page intent with an embedded profile is included here.

cases.source_location: Table 166 physical p. 485 / printed p. 470: a stored appearance stream makes annotation CA/ca inapplicable; the appearance stream specifies transparency. Issue #51 is at physical p. 997 / printed p. 982 in Annex Q and adds the BM transparency condition; it does not modify the CA rule. Annex Q.1 says the method is normative where used, while noting PDF 2.0 does not generally require every processor to run this determination method.
cases.fixture: crates/pdf-archive/tests/transparency_detection_spec_audit.rs::annotation_ca_does_not_override_an_explicit_opaque_appearance and annotation_bm_still_marks_an_explicit_appearance_transparent. Exact-xref PDF 2.0 has IDs, page Annots, AcroForm Fields, valid Pushbutton widget /Ff 65536, /P, /Rect, and explicit /AP /N Form stream with /BBox and Resources. CA=.5, CA=1, CA absent, and annotation BM=/Multiply vary independently; the Form AP is otherwise opaque. The helper asserts no xref recovery, and survey.stopped_short is false.
cases.fixture_validity: Valid PDF 2.0 non-markup Widget annotation: Table 166 permits CA for non-markup annotations, and expressly says it shall not be used with an appearance stream. Explicit /NeedAppearances false avoids appearance-regeneration ambiguity. BM is permitted in PDF 2.0 and Issue #51 specifically adds non-Normal BM detection.
cases.oracle: Public Survey::page_is_transparent is directly compared against the deterministic binary classifications false/true. Absent CA and CA=1 opaque controls establish ordinary behavior; the independent BM=/Multiply control must be transparent. Survey internals additionally have an existing appearance-stream CA=0.25 versus CA=1 control showing an AP's own ExtGState is traversed; this distinguishes annotation dictionary CA from graphics-state CA inside the AP.
cases.execution: transparency-final-wave30d.log and later full waves: absent CA, CA=1 and BM positive control pass; CA=.5 with opaque AP is falsely reported transparent.
cases.decision_recheck: The finding is properly scoped to the archive's deliberate Annex-Q transparency survey and consumers of that report; it is not a claim that all PDF 2.0 processors must implement Annex Q. Within a survey using Q, Table 166 disallows treating stored-AP CA as the appearance's graphics-state opacity. The #51 overlay concerns BM only.
cases.residuals: No full PDF/A conformance verdict or screen rendering defect is inferred. The test uses the Survey abstraction rather than a complete PDF/A checker; any downstream impact is limited to consumers of its transparency result.
